name: Saint Mary's Chinese Mission
note: 1900s Classical Revival mission church, cream, entrance colonnade, hip roof.

name: Ripley's Believe It or Not
note: Fisherman's Wharf attraction. 2026-10-17 land-side audit: was ripleysBelieveItOrNot (civic-1.ts; a pale-blue mural band on plain red walls that read as a blue box). Now ripleys (wharf-landside.ts): the scalloped arcade of red flaring piers and arch rings over the roof, the San Francisco mural (Golden Gate, XING, Palace of Fine Arts) on sky blue, the yellow script name, Applebee's apple on the Taylor arches, the silver fan-arch marquee and Wharf Central (Mapillary 1313734760314896, 195540726374305, 747140704615642). 2026-10-17 (owner's Street View of 155 Jefferson looking along to Ripley's): the ground floor cut OPEN on both streets; the east bays are PACIFIC FAIR SHOPS under a grey shingled hood with a teal fascia, HOODY 2 for $20 / HOODY for $20 boards, racks and a postcard spinner (which bays: GUESSED); the marquee moved to mid-front with a RIPLEYS blade; WHARF CENTRAL open; APPLEBEE'S red-framed glass corner where the red arcade begins next to Pacific Fair (Mapillary 1289359246072032 and the owner's frame show Applebee's name at the arcade's east end; its OSM node/address are on Taylor); a Believe It or Not! billboard painted on the blank east wall over 155's roof (GUESSED).

name: Gold Mountain Monastery
note: 2026-10-16: the outline is also Bank of America's Chinatown branch at 701 Grant — the pagoda-eaved corner with red columns the street sees (Mapillary); notable.ts grantSacramentoCorner. Was: goldMountainMonastery: 800 Sacramento St, ex-mattress-factory building bought 1970: 3-storey cream Chinatown facade, pagoda-eaved corner tower. Levels counted from photo: 3.

name: Mount Zion Baptist Church
note: 1906 wood-frame church at Oak/Baker; identity confirmed by web search (photo obscured by trees/neighbouring Victorians). Modest nave, one level, small bell tower.

name: Edwin and Anita Lee Newcomer School
note: 657 Merchant St, ordinary stone-faced school block. Levels counted from photo: 4 (ground + 3 upper, fire escape visible).

name: City College of San Francisco Chinatown Annex
note: 628 Washington St, the 4-storey annex beside the Colombo Building (EHDD's 15-storey tower is a separate OSM way). Plain brick.

name: Nourse Theater
note: 275 Hayes St, 1926 John Reid Jr., ex-Commerce High School auditorium. ONE level (auditorium), carved terracotta Spanish Revival entrance surround.

name: San Francisco Fire Station 35
note: Pier 22 1/2 Fireboat House, 1915 Alfred A. Pyle: white Mission/Renaissance Revival, tile hip roof. Levels counted from photo: 2.

name: Notre Dame Des Victoires Church
note: 566 Bush St, 1915 French Romanesque: ochre terracotta, round apse, campanile with pyramidal spire on the corner.

name: National Maritime Museum
note: Aquatic Park Bathhouse, 1939 William Mooser Jr., Streamline Moderne: white ship-shaped building, curved prow, deck-rail parapet, mast group on the rounded pilot house.

name: San Francisco Unified School District Administration
note: Old High School of Commerce (building:levels=3), cream Classical Revival, matches its neighbour the Nourse Theater; entrance colonnade.

name: 501 Fulton Street
note: Jehovah's Witness Kingdom Hall; plain low meeting hall, reference photo aimed at a neighbouring modern building so kept as a simple restyle.

name: San Francisco Transition Structure
note: Transbay Tube ventilation/transition building (building:levels=3, roof=quadruple_saltbox): plain brick transit box under a saltbox-like hip roof.
